_readme: Narrow candidate pools for the CHARACTER dialect (humanoid deform rig + FaceFX facial rig).
THESE POOLS ARE DELIBERATELY SMALL. Expected false positives = S * T / 2^32. A big vocabulary is
self-defeating: a chance hit into a large dictionary READS like a real name and destroys the only
witness we have. Every pool below has been RUN and returned ZERO (see doc section 5). They are kept
so nobody re-tests them, and so a future source can be matched against the right grammar.
BEFORE ADDING ANYTHING, APPLY THE THREE FREE FILTERS IN 'laws' BELOW. They cost nothing and they
kill most candidates outright -- including, provably, every candidate any previous attack ever

parity_law.statement: bit0(m2(name)) == bit0(FNV_OFFSET) XOR parity(number of ODD bytes in the name after |0x20).
parity_law.why: FNV-1a: the prime is odd so multiplication preserves bit 0, and XOR feeds bit 0 straight through.
parity_law.corollary: 'l'=0x6C and 'r'=0x72 are BOTH EVEN, so a glued l<->r rename cannot change hash bit 0. Any glued l/r mirror pair MUST agree in bit 0. Verified 11/11 on the known pairs of the 105-bone rig.
parity_law.use_as: A free 1-bit filter on EVERY candidate: required_odd_byte_parity = 1 XOR (hash & 1).

mirror_sieve.statement: Every FNV-1a byte step is invertible, so a mirror pair's shared STEM can be solved for WITHOUT knowing the prefix: unwind STEM then the side token from both hashes; a true stem makes both land on the SAME prefix-state s0.
mirror_sieve.payoff: The recovered s0 identifies the prefix as a SEPARATE 32-bit problem, so the name factors into two independent facts instead of one. Positive controls: recovers 'bicep' from bone_l/rbicep and fold('bone_cheek_') from bone_cheek_left/right, prefix withheld.

length_gate.statement: Stem characters XOR into both sides of a mirror pair identically, so they cancel out of the LOW BITS of the consistency value. Those bits depend only on the two hashes and the stem's LENGTH -- so a stem LENGTH can be refused for free, at any length, enumerating nothing.

proven_exclusions.trk3_trk10: NOT a glued l/r mirror pair -- hash bit0 differs (1 vs 0). PROOF, any stem, any length, any prefix. Also excluded: <any>left<stem<=6>, <any>lft<stem<=6>. Their bind-pose local offsets are NOT mirror images either -- trk3/trk10 are probably not a name-mirror pair at all. bone_forge.py's SLOTS asserts they are; that assertion is wrong.
proven_exclusions.trk54_trk76: glued-l/r consistent, but NO stem of <=6 chars exists behind ANY prefix (2.64e9 stems sieved, zero survivors). Stem is >=7 chars.
proven_exclusions.trk28_trk31: same: no glued-l/r stem <=6 behind any prefix. Stem is >=7 chars.
proven_exclusions.all_three_pairs: No pair ends in a side token (12 spellings checked, expected-false 2.3e-10 each). Side is MEDIAL. => the FaceFX Convention-C grammar bone_<feature>_<side> is EXCLUDED for the jaw pair trk28/31.
proven_exclusions.saboteur_face_rig: Does NOT transfer. 79 mined literals + 42,442 re-spellings vs all 8,561 unnamed hashes, expected-false <=0.085, ZERO hits. The sibling game gives a concept checklist, never a literal Mercs2 face string.

mined_literals._source_body: output/_ghidra_saboteur/saboteur_all_functions_decomp.txt -- args to the find-bone-by-name helper FUN_00db7e10(const char*, int)
mined_literals._note_bone_bone1: Bone_bone1 is a DCC DEFAULT AUTO-NAME shipped into a retail Pandemic rig. It is PROOF that these riggers leave non-lexical tokens in the skeleton -- the same class as Mercs2's bone_ub / bone_lb. It is the shape of the remaining unknowns, and it is why a bigger dictionary cannot help.
mined_literals._source_face: /c/GOG Games/The Saboteur/FaceFX/{Male,Female}.fxa -- the complete FxMasterBoneList (36 bones)
mined_literals._curve_note: Stock OC3 FaceFX curve names. Curves drive bones; they are NOT bones and never appear in a HIER. Do not hash them against bone hashes.
mined_literals.hash_result: ALL of the above tested verbatim against all 8,561 unnamed census hashes: expected-false 0.00016, ZERO hits.

deform_vocab._grammar: bone_ <side(l|r, GLUED, prefix)> <part> <twist?> <num?>   -- CamelCase-ish, side glued to the part. Casing is evidentially VOID (the hash folds |0x20).
deform_vocab._status: Confirmed by 208 witnessed names AND by The Saboteur's identical literals. The grammar is right; the vocabulary is the wall.

facefx_vocab._grammar: bone_<feature>[_<position>]_<side>  -- snake_case, descriptive, side TRAILING as a FULL WORD (left|right|center). l/r is NEVER used on a FaceFX bone.
facefx_vocab._status: Regenerates all 20 confirmed facial bones at expected-false 0.000 (positive control passes). It produces NOTHING for the 8 head/jaw unknowns -- and section 3.1 of the doc PROVES why for trk28/31: that pair does not end in a side token, so it is not this grammar at all.
facefx_vocab._control_layer_status: All tested. ZERO hits. Saboteur HAS this control layer (Bone_HeadBase / Bone_MouthBase / Bone_JawBone); Mercs2 spells its equivalents differently or not at all.

geometric_witnesses._source: docs/data/bone_skeleton.csv, model 0x03C70F0A. NOTE: the parent/depth columns of that CSV are UNRELIABLE for these models (self-contradictory rows). The wx/wy/wz LOCAL bind offsets are self-consistent and are what these readings use.
geometric_witnesses.mirror_axis_is_per_parent: bone_cheek_left/right mirror in z (head-space); bone_mouth_bottom_left/right mirror in x (jaw-space). Pick the axis from the parent, not globally.
geometric_witnesses.trk28_trk31: (+0.0241,-0.0864,+0.0814) / (-0.0239,-0.0864,+0.0814) -- mirror in x sharing z, the exact signature of bone_mouth_bottom_left/right. Jaw children, ~6cm BELOW the mouth-bottom bones: the CHIN / JAWLINE band. trk28=+x=LEFT, trk31=-x=RIGHT. INFERENCE, not a crack.
geometric_witnesses.trk29_30_32_33: ~(0,0,+0.02) each -- four near-identical MIDLINE bones each ~2cm forward of its parent = a serial midline chain. The only serial midline chain in a head is the TONGUE (bone_tongue_tip sits further along at (0,-0.0276,+0.0565)). INFERENCE, not a crack -- the full tongue/teeth vocabulary incl. misspellings returned zero.
geometric_witnesses.trk3_trk10: (+0.1544,+0.0336,-0.0118) / (0.0000,+0.0256,-0.0921) -- NOT mirror images. Corroborates the parity proof that these two are not an l/r name pair.

notes: ZERO new names were cracked this session. Everything above is either MINED (literal, certain) or PROVEN NEGATIVE (m2 is deterministic, so a miss is an exclusion).

THE ESCAPE HATCH IS CLOSED. Both earlier dialect docs conclude the route to these names is 'an unstripped dev/debug build'. We HAVE one -- the Jul-11-2008 devkit prototype with a real PDB (output/jul08_prototype/) -- and a full string sweep of it yields only the 25 bone literals we ALREADY knew. The missing names are not in it.

DO NOT run a wider blind sweep. Coverage is already solved (the prior <=13-char exhaustive sweep covers bone_l + 7 chars and returned ~70,000 chance hits). Recognition is the wall, and a wider dictionary makes recognition strictly WORSE because a chance hit into a big dictionary reads like a real name.
DO use the three laws above before generating anything -- they are free and they are proofs. In particular, the parity law retroactively invalidates every candidate ever generated for trk3/trk10.

The remaining routes are all EXTERNAL: a Pandemic .max/.ma source rig, an exporter script, an art-side naming doc, or a build with the bone-name string table intact. Until one appears, keep these 15 as hashes -- the engine addresses bones by hash anyway, so nothing is blocked.
A WRONG NAME IS WORSE THAN AN UNKNOWN ONE. Never accept a lone hit from a wide sweep.
